newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity lower as Jan goes off the board.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity lower as Jan goes off the board.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures closed lower Thursday amid relatively warm temperatures in the western U.S. and plentiful hydroelectric supplies, market sources said.
Weaker natural gas prices were also cited as putting downward pressure on the power market.
Traders noted relatively few outstanding January California-Oregon border (COB) and Palo Verde (PV) futures were traded ahead of the contracts' expiration at Thursday's close.
"Open interest for both (January COB and PV) was around 400 lots, but only around 60 PV and 140 COB were sold," said one dealer.
"Apparently a large number are going to delivery," he added.
Sources speculated that a lot of players got caught long in the course of January's sharp drop in price over the past couple of weeks.
"I guess they decided going to delivery was the lesser of two evils," said one trader.
January 1997 California-Oregon border (COB) futures lost 64 cents to close at $18.15 per megawatt hour (MWh), while the February contract was down $1.33 at $16.17.
Other active COB contracts were down by 50 to 75 cents.
January Palo Verde fell $2.07 to expire at $19.93 per MWh, while February was down $1.00 at $17.00.
Other PV contracts were down 35 cents to $1.10.
